stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Inside Microsoft’s big Copilot rethink
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is fundamentally rethinking its Copilot offering.
The new vision positions Copilot as the 'OS for work,' indicating a deep integration strategy.
The announcement was made via an exclusive, high-level customer event rather than a broad media launch.

stories.title: OpenAI’s new agent is a shot at Meta — but can it compete with free?
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI unveiled 'Dots,' a new AI agent powered by GPT-6 Astra, at its DevDay conference.
The launch is positioned as a direct competitive move against Meta's successful Muse AI agent platform.
The announcement signals OpenAI's aggressive push to develop sophisticated, real-world AI agents.

stories.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Critical vulnerability found in Zimbra email software.
Exploitation allows attackers to remotely inject operating system commands.
The attack vector can be triggered via a simple email.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has unveiled a new AI model named Gemini 4 Argon.
The new model is positioned as a successor or advancement over Gemini 3.5 Pro.
The model is not yet available for public use.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The context is within the text-generation pipeline, relevant to LLM deployment and fine-tuning.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The pipeline indicates its primary use case is 'text-generation'.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model is optimized for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon utilizing MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Speedups reach up to 90% when running coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs and faster response times.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Judge dismisses antitrust lawsuits over Google’s AI Overviews
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Federal judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits against Google regarding its AI Overviews.
The lawsuits, filed by Chegg and Penske Media Corporation, alleged Google was harming web traffic.
Judge Amit Mehta ruled in favor of Google in the antitrust case concerning AI search features.

stories.title: Sony brings AI graphics upscaling to the regular PS5
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Sony is integrating a new AI upscaling technology, Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), into the standard PS5.
The technology is a result of Sony's 'Project Amethyst' collaboration with AMD.
This represents a new performance tier for AI upscaling on the PlayStation platform.

stories.title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Introduces Cogentic, a multi-agent orchestration harness designed for automated proof discovery.
Addresses the limitations of single-shot language model generation when tackling complex, open mathematical problems.
Employs an iterative prove-verify loop to manage long-horizon tasks, explore competing conjectures, and overcome technical obstructions.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws,' a novel framework to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by combining the effects of recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) in a single model.
The work proposes a 'sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping' to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact with model size and data.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws,' a novel framework to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
Suggests a new direction for efficient large-scale model training by integrating the benefits of recurrent structures and sparse activation.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (27.5% to 31.1%) of real-world web text is now being generated by AI models.
This 'wild' AI text is challenging because it is unlabeled, comes from diverse models, and is intended for human consumption.
The research investigates the impact of this pervasive, unlabeled AI-generated content on the pretraining process of large language models.

stories.title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
stories.author: Dongyeop Kang
bullet_points: Introduces EvoDuet, a novel bi-level optimization method for scientific discovery.
Addresses the limitation of LLMs stalling when external knowledge is required during search/solving tasks.
Co-evolves solutions and search queries simultaneously, using a retrieval gate to manage knowledge gaps.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
stories.author: Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loop Scaling Laws' to jointly model the scaling behavior of Looped Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE).
Addresses a gap in current research by modeling recurrence (depth) and sparsity (capacity) simultaneously, rather than in isolation.
The work presents a novel, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping to understand how these two efficient scaling techniques interact.

stories.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
stories.author: Bradley Emi
bullet_points: A significant portion (27.5% to 31.1%) of real-world web text is increasingly being generated by AI models.
The study investigates the impact of this 'wild' AI-generated text—which is unlabeled and comes from diverse models—on language model pretraining.
The research addresses the growing concern over data contamination and the quality of training corpora in the age of generative AI.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports integration with Ollama.
This integration allows users to utilize open-source models through Claude.
Ollama functions as a third-party gateway provider for this functionality.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Can VR glasses save VR?
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has released new VR glasses, signaling a potential shift in the VR market.
The high price point ($1,299) is noted as a barrier to mass consumer adoption.
The device is described as a significant leap forward in VR hardware capabilities.

stories.title: Inside our months-long investigation into Kevin O’Leary’s Utah data center debacle
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: The story investigates Kevin O'Leary's plan to develop a massive data center in Utah.
The proposed facility is described as a 40,000-acre AI campus.
The project requires a substantial power capacity of nine gigawatts.

stories.title: PS5 emulation is suddenly making big strides on PC
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: PS5 emulation is showing significant performance improvements on PC.
Titles such as Astro Bot and Demon's Souls are now running well via emulation.
This development signals a growing capability in console emulation technology.

stories.title: Returning from vacation? The government can search your phone without a warrant.
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: The article discusses a legal loophole allowing government searches of phones at borders without a warrant.
This relates to the 'border exemption' which limits certain constitutional rights in specific contexts.
It serves as a warning to readers regarding potential surveillance powers at entry points.

stories.title: A local network of implants uses your body as the wiring
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: Research demonstrates the feasibility of transmitting electrical signals directly through human tissues.
The concept involves using the human body itself as a conduit or wiring system for implants.
This technology suggests potential for advanced, minimally invasive bio-interfacing devices.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to irrelevant prompt features, even when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
The study introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test and analyze this sensitivity while maintaining the core problem's integrity.
The findings suggest that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can effectively improve the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The paper introduces ViTeX-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating high-fidelity video scene text editing.
The research addresses the gap in video editing capabilities, specifically focusing on precise local edits that maintain scene dynamics.
Scene text editing involves replacing text on surfaces (like signs or labels) within a video while preserving surrounding motion and camera dynamics.

stories.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces 'Turbo Harness,' a new framework for optimizing AI agent harnesses.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods that use a single, uniform harness across all task instances.
Turbo Harness adapts a globally optimized harness to individual instances by reusing prior optimization data.

stories.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Shiyu Chang
bullet_points: Introduces WorldAuditBench, a new framework for auditing interactive 3D simulated environments.
The goal is to automatically detect anomalies (e.g., floating objects, inconsistent geometry) within these complex 3D worlds.
Leverages multimodal AI systems, specifically VLMs and VLAs, to automate the challenging task of 3D world auditing.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It uses alpha-masked layers and pretrained language models to explicitly define dependencies between material patterns, color, and relief for PBR rendering.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the challenge of long-horizon robot manipulation by bridging semantic reasoning and physical execution.
It introduces a dynamic physical harness that coordinates these two disparate timescales (coarse semantic vs. fine physical interaction).
The system utilizes a shared execution contract to guide self-evolution, improving upon limited guidance from episode-level failures.

stories.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
stories.author: Emmanuel Abbé
bullet_points: Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) agents are advancing, but face stagnation issues in long-horizon tasks.
Current advanced MLE agents rely on complex 'harnesses' like multi-agent orchestrators and retrieval subagents.
The paper suggests exploring simpler, more primitive coding agents with direct execution access as a potential path forward.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical flaw in current clinical AI: reliance on accuracy metrics in class-imbalanced medical data.
Proposes optimizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) using AUROC instead of simple accuracy for better clinical relevance.
Focuses on 'Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization' as a novel technique to improve diagnostic performance in MLLMs.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to task-irrelevant features in prompts, even when using verifiable rewards (RLVR).
Introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how much LLM predictions rely on non-essential prompt details.
Proposes a decoding improvement—suppressing high-drift token candidates—which demonstrably enhances reasoning accuracy.

stories.title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: Research challenges the reproducibility of reported improvements in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding.
The study suggests that claimed gains might be artifacts of specific data processing techniques, such as fixed-length windowing and overlapping segments.
The findings imply that some reported advancements in BCI (Brain-Computer Interface) technology may rely on 'timing shortcuts' rather than fundamental decoding improvements.

stories.title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
stories.author: Abir Das
bullet_points: Introduces VideoMSN, a Masked Siamese Network for self-supervised spatio-temporal video representation learning.
Avoids heavy 3D architectures and reconstruction-based autoencoders by repurposing standard image Vision Transformers.
Videos are treated as 'super images' (grids of sampled frames) to create two views for masking (spatial and temporal).

stories.title: Is Weight Tying Still Beneficial for Decoder-Only LLMs in Private Settings Under DP-SGD?
stories.author: Razane Tajeddine
bullet_points: The research investigates the impact of weight tying (a common LLM design choice) when fine-tuning decoder-only LLMs using Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD).
Weight tying is typically used for parameter efficiency and performance in standard LLM training, but its behavior under privacy constraints is unknown.
This work addresses a gap in the literature regarding the interaction between architectural design (weight tying) and privacy-preserving training methods (DP-SGD).

stories.title: Compression Footprints as Security Signals for Model-Poisoning Defense in Federated Learning
stories.author: William Eiers
bullet_points: Proposes using 'compression footprints' as a novel security signal in Federated Learning (FL) to detect model poisoning.
Challenges the conventional approach of treating lossy compression solely as an error source in FL.
Suggests that the distortion and payload behavior induced by compression can differentiate between honest and malicious model updates.

stories.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: DynaHarness addresses the challenge of long-horizon robot manipulation by bridging the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level physical execution.
It proposes a dynamic physical harness that uses a shared execution contract to couple these two disparate systems.
The framework aims to improve robot learning by providing better guidance from episode failures, moving beyond simple action priors.

stories.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
stories.author: Gao Huang
bullet_points: Proposes 'Looped Diffusion Transformer' as an alternative scaling method for text-to-image models.
Increases computational depth by repeatedly running shared Transformer blocks within each denoising step, without increasing parameter count.
Aims to enable iterative refinement of internal representations, potentially improving image quality without explicit reasoning tokens.

stories.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
stories.author: Jiayun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in clinical AI: standard accuracy metrics fail with imbalanced medical data.
Proposes optimizing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) using AUROC, a ranking-aware metric, instead of simple accuracy.
Focuses on prompt optimization techniques to improve the clinical utility and robustness of MLLMs in diagnosis.

stories.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yue Zhang
bullet_points: Investigates the sensitivity of Large Language Models (LLMs) to task-irrelevant prompt features, even when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
Introduces 'semifactual prompt interventions' to test how much LLM predictions vary when only the core problem and answer are preserved.
Proposes that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding can enhance the reasoning accuracy of LLMs.

stories.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
stories.author: Michael R. Lyu
bullet_points: Introduces MatLoom, a new compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation.
The system generates not just appearance, but also the underlying construction rules for materials.
It uses alpha-masked layers and pretrained language models to explicitly define dependencies between patterns, color, and PBR channels.

stories.title: Linguistic Loopholes in LLM Unlearning: From a 174-Language Benchmark to Coverage-Aware Unlearning
stories.author: Abhay Yadav
bullet_points: Identifies a critical 'cross-lingual loophole' in LLM unlearning, where forgetting a fact in one language doesn't guarantee its removal in others.
Proposes 'language budgeted multilingual unlearning' as a scalable alternative to the impractical solution of unlearning across all languages.
Addresses the trade-off between ensuring complete knowledge removal and preventing collateral damage to unrelated model capabilities.

stories.title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
stories.author: Jing Yu Koh
bullet_points: Computer Use Agents (CUAs) are showing impressive performance, sometimes exceeding human capabilities on complex tasks.
A major hurdle for CUA adoption is their current speed and operational cost.
The paper introduces 'cua-speedrun' to provide standardized and reproducible benchmarking for CUA speed.

stories.title: Decision-Oriented Recommendation Reranking: An Empirical Study of Jev
stories.author: Yinglong Xia
bullet_points: The research addresses the trade-off between recommendation quality and serving efficiency when using Large Language Models (LLMs) for reranking.
It proposes and empirically investigates a 'decision-oriented model' (Jev) as an alternative for structured choice tasks in personalized recommendations.
The study focuses on evaluating a 'System One Model' approach against standard LLM usage in the context of recommendation systems.

stories.title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports
stories.author: Hari Trivedi
bullet_points: The research compares fine-tuning an open-weight model (Gemma-3-12B) against proprietary models (like GPT-4o) for entity extraction from radiology reports.
The study addresses critical industry concerns regarding privacy, cost, and reproducibility associated with proprietary clinical AI tools.
The specific task evaluated is multi-label intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) acuity extraction from non-contrast head-CT reports.

stories.title: ELI5: Why can hiding one sentence inside a web page make an AI ignore its own owner and obey a total stranger?
stories.author: rudratosh
bullet_points: The article explores a vulnerability where subtle text manipulation (hiding one sentence) can trick AI models.
This manipulation allows the AI to disregard its original instructions or 'owner' and follow commands from an external source.
The topic is highly relevant to AI safety, prompt injection, and model security.

stories.title: How to add Live Web Search to an AI Agent
stories.author: unicodeveloper
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical need for AI agents to perform live web searches.
A key feature discussed is the ability for agents to inspect real-time sources.
The importance of citation is highlighted for ensuring answer accuracy and traceability.
